hook.text: In 2015, hackers accessed 700,000 taxpayer accounts through the IRS 'Get Transcript' tool.

buildup.text: The attackers used data bought on the dark web—SSNs, addresses, birthdates.

discovery.text: The stolen transcripts contained enough information to file fraudulent returns and claim refunds.

twist.text: The IRS blamed 'sophisticated criminals.' But security researchers said the verification was embarrassingly weak.

climax.text: The breach showed that the IRS holds the most sensitive financial data in America.

punchline.text: 700,000 accounts breached. Questions you could Google.

quiz.question: How did hackers access 700,000 IRS taxpayer accounts in 2015?
options: They used stolen personal data to pass weak identity verification
An IRS employee gave them access
